topic.angle: An ancient Greek gear device found in a shipwreck that tracked the sky

card.title: The gears that came too early

body.question: The Antikythera mechanism, a geared sky-tracker from the 2nd century BC, was a wonder. How long before machines of similar complexity appeared again?
body.reveal: Machines of similar complexity did not appear again for around 1,500 years, with early examples being 14th-century astronomical clocks. The Antikythera mechanism was hand-powered and could predict astronomical positions and eclipses decades in advance. It came from a shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera, retrieved in 1901.

probes.question: True or false: the Antikythera mechanism could also track the four-year cycle of athletic games like the ancient Olympics.
In which year was the Antikythera mechanism discovered?

image_brief.show: The corroded bronze fragments of the Antikythera mechanism in the National Archaeological Museum, Athens
